topics.title: Nature of stress
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; Nature, Types and Sources of Stress; Nature of Stress

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish eustress from distress and explain stress as a pattern of responses to demands that exceed coping ability.
Explain Lazarus's primary and secondary appraisal and the harm, threat and challenge appraisals of an event.
Describe stress reactions and how intensity, duration, complexity and predictability shape the outcome of stress.

topics.title: Types and sources of stress
topics.ncert_sections: Types of Stress; Sources of Stress; Box 3.1

concepts.learning_objective: Identify physical and environmental, psychological and social stress with examples.
Explain frustration, conflict, internal pressure and social pressure as sources of psychological stress.
Distinguish life events, daily hassles and traumatic events and interpret life event measures of stress.

topics.title: Effects of stress on psychological functioning
topics.ncert_sections: Effects of Stress on Psychological Functioning and Health; Box 3.2

concepts.learning_objective: Classify emotional, physiological, cognitive and behavioural effects of stress.
Explain how examination anxiety can help or impair a student's performance.
Define burnout as a state of physical, emotional and psychological exhaustion.

topics.title: Stress and health
topics.ncert_sections: Stress and Health; General Adaptation Syndrome; Stress and the Immune System; Lifestyle

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the alarm reaction, resistance and exhaustion stages of Selye's General Adaptation Syndrome.
Explain how stress impairs the immune system, as studied by psychoneuroimmunology.
Analyse how stress leads to health-damaging lifestyle behaviours.
Distinguish the task-oriented, emotion-oriented and avoidance-oriented coping strategies of Endler and Parker.
Differentiate problem-focused and emotion-focused coping as described by Lazarus and Folkman.
Describe relaxation, meditation and the stages of biofeedback training.
Explain the aim and phases of Meichenbaum's stress inoculation training.
Explain how creative visualisation and exercise help to manage stress.

topics.title: Hardiness and life skills
topics.ncert_sections: Promoting Positive Health and Well-being; Life Skills

concepts.learning_objective: Explain Kobasa's stress resistant personality and its three Cs: commitment, control and challenge.
Identify life skills such as assertiveness, time management, rational thinking, improving relationships and self-care.
Recognise perfectionism, avoidance and procrastination as unhelpful habits that increase vulnerability to stress.
Explain resilience and its I HAVE, I AM and I CAN resources.
Explain how diet, exercise, positive attitude and optimism act as stress buffers.
Distinguish tangible, informational and emotional social support and explain their effect on well-being.
